solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Give a hand to lad playing with a pup

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are messing about and landing in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy romping with a puppy, while someone is asked to clap him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges LAD, A and PUP together; 'with' only joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To applaud someone is to clap them, idiomatically to give them a hand.

clue.text: What solicitors do to remain available?

definitions.meaning: people who solicit ask for things, so this is what beggars and touts do
something left unclaimed and on offer to anyone is said to be going this way

explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitors' reads as lawyers, but here it means anyone who solicits, that is, asks or begs.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom covers both pleading for things and an item lying unclaimed for whoever wants it.

parts.note: Ben is a boy's name
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A boy and a girl have a meeting down by the bay.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bay of Bengal lies east of India; 'meets' and 'in' simply join the pieces and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bay of Bengal is the large bay of the Indian Ocean east of India, so its name stands for it.

clue.text: Prying person occupied with main part

parts.note: occupied means busy, having things to do
the body of something is its main part, as the body of a letter

explanation.surface: A nosy individual who keeps occupied with the bulk of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A busybody is a meddler who pries into the affairs of others.

clue.text: East London passage that has a dark side?

definitions.text: East London passage that has a dark side?

parts.words: East London passage that has a dark side?
parts.note: a road tunnel under the Thames in east London whose name, read literally, describes a side that is a dark wall

explanation.walkthrough: The Blackwall Tunnel runs under the Thames in east London; its name split up suggests a black wall.
explanation.definitionFit: The Blackwall Tunnel is a pair of road tunnels beneath the Thames in east London.

clue.text: Get rid of mum's wig on holiday

parts.note: to keep mum is to stay quiet, and sh is the call for quiet
rug is slang for a wig or toupee
someone on holiday is off work

explanation.surface: Mother tries to dispose of her hairpiece while away on vacation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum's' looks like mother's, but it gives SH, the hushing sound, from keeping mum.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrug something off is to dismiss or throw it off, a synonym for getting rid of it.

clue.text: Exclude two leading raiders from Scottish island

parts.note: to bar someone is to exclude them

indicators.note: two leading means the opening pair of letters of the next word are taken

explanation.surface: Keeping the front pair of raiders off an island in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two leading' takes RA, the first two letters of 'raiders'.
explanation.definitionFit: Barra is an island in the Outer Hebrides off the west coast of Scotland.

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters are scattered through the air and land in another order

explanation.surface: Refuse collectors sending mud everywhere as they work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges the letters of SENT MUD.
explanation.definitionFit: Dustmen are refuse collectors, traditionally employed by the local council in Britain.

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
to model is to pose

explanation.surface: A kitchen counter worktop being modelled for a photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter' reads as a noun, but it is the verb meaning resist; 'by' simply puts the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To counter a proposal is to resist or speak against it.

clue.text: Look before groom gets to tone down photograph

indicators.note: before means the first piece is placed ahead of the next one

parts.note: an air is a look or manner someone has
to brush a horse is to groom it

explanation.surface: Someone checks their appearance before the bridegroom retouches a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groom' suggests a bridegroom, but it is the verb to brush.
explanation.definitionFit: To airbrush a photograph is to retouch it, softening or toning down features.

clue.text: Grace ill prepared for this reaction

definitions.text: Grace ill prepared for this reaction

indicators.note: something prepared has been worked up into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Poor Grace was not ready for how her body responded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges GRACE ILL; the whole clue also describes someone suffering an allergic attack.
explanation.definitionFit: An allergic reaction is the body's response to something it is sensitive to, as Grace's illness suggests.

clue.text: Weight that's just the same without me

definitions.text: Weight that's just the same without me

parts.words: Weight that's just the same without me
parts.note: a unit of mass that is spelt two ways, the shorter one being the longer with its last two letters, M and E, dropped

explanation.walkthrough: The longer spelling of this metric unit means exactly the same once its final ME is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: The gramme is a metric unit of mass, alternatively spelt gram.

parts.note: to bung something is to chuck or throw it
humble means low in rank

explanation.surface: A man named Chuck owns a modest home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chuck' looks like a man's name but is the verb to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A bungalow is a one-storey house, a type of residential property.

parts.note: alpha is the NATO alphabet word for A
articulate means fluent in speech

explanation.surface: A dominant woman who speaks well and is doing well.
explanation.definitionFit: Affluent means wealthy, which is a synonym for prosperous.

parts.note: read as a metro line below ground, then as the verb for emphasising a word

explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is London's underground railway; an underground line is the joke, and stressing words is the real sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To underline something is to stress or emphasise it.

parts.note: describes a lack of religious conviction, having no trust in religion itself

explanation.walkthrough: The second 'faith' means a religion, so the clue describes doubting religion altogether.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbelief is the absence of belief, especially of religious faith.

clue.text: First to take one drink into examination

indicators.note: into means one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
the Roman numeral I is one
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: A candidate taking a drink into an exam for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' is the container signal; 'First' is the definition and 'to take' only joins it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Original means first, the earliest of its kind.

definitions.meaning: a French island east of Madagascar in the Indian Ocean
a gathering of people who have been apart

explanation.walkthrough: Spelt with an accent on the E in French, the island's name is the same as the English word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the spelling: the island east of Madagascar and a get-together of old friends.

clue.text: Declare English taken in by one seeking retribution

indicators.note: taken in by means the first piece is held inside the next one

parts.note: to aver is to declare

explanation.surface: An Englishman tricked by someone out for revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' is the container signal: the abbreviation sits inside the verb for declare.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenger is someone who takes revenge, seeking retribution for a wrong.

parts.note: if the lower part weighs little, then the upper part must weigh a lot

explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes first; the rest is a cryptic hint at the opposite end bearing the weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Something top-heavy is unbalanced because too much weight sits above.

indicators.note: held means the second piece is kept inside the first

parts.note: pacy means fast, moving quickly
taken as written

explanation.surface: Settle down quickly if you are being held.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held' is the container signal; 'quickly' must become an adjective meaning fast, a slight stretch the clue allows.
explanation.definitionFit: To pacify someone is to soothe or calm them down.

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, a Frenchman

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or obscure, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a Frenchman has a set of crossword hints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might' looks like a verb opening a question, but it is the noun meaning strength; 'cryptic' rearranges CLUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscle means physical power or strength, a synonym for might.

parts.note: a nation that shares its name with porcelain, which cracks easily

explanation.walkthrough: The nation's name also means porcelain crockery, which cracks.
explanation.definitionFit: China is a country, and china is fragile porcelain prone to cracking.

clue.text: Eyebrows may rise when it's plunging

definitions.text: Eyebrows may rise when it's plunging

parts.words: Eyebrows may rise when it's plunging
parts.note: a garment's edge at the top that, cut low, shocks onlookers

explanation.walkthrough: A plunging edge on a dress is cut very low; rising and plunging are a playful contrast.
explanation.definitionFit: The neckline is the edge of a garment around the neck, and a plunging one is cut daringly low.

definitions.meaning: a split is a separation or rift
an army formation of several brigades

explanation.definitionFit: Division means both a separation into parts and a large military unit.

indicators.note: behind means this piece follows the previous one

parts.note: a fen is a marsh or bog

indicators.note: back means the name is read from right to left

parts.note: Len is short for Leonard

explanation.surface: Leonard returns to find a plant behind the marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' is the reversal signal on the short name, and 'behind' places the turned name after the marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Fennel is an aromatic plant used as a herb and vegetable.

clue.text: Banned peacekeepers start to look terrible

parts.note: the UN provides peacekeeping forces

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: awful means terrible

explanation.surface: Barred peacekeepers are beginning to look dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to' takes L, the first letter of 'look'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unlawful is illegal, forbidden or banned by law.
